reason: The apex (mouth) of a leaf sheath, typically in grasses and sedges ('hyaline', 'oblique'). It is expressed as the apex region of leaf sheath, as for other organ apices. 'sheath' is already a context-word bearer in flora_context_words.
A positioned part: the end pinna of a pinnate leaf or frond. 'terminal' already lists pinna in flora_context_words. It parallels the existing positioned part terminal leaflet (FLOPO_0996015).
The apex of an inflorescence bract. Using the apex region keeps the more specific bract. The broader bract apex (PO_0025154) is the fallback.
Exact: a hyphenated spelling of the PO label. These are the papilionaceous keel petals ('falcate', 'apiculate'), not a ridge.

Exact: the midrib of a moss leaf. 'excurrent' and 'percurrent' are moss terms, and PO already lists phyllid costa as a synonym. In vascular-plant descriptions the vascular leaf costa is a synonym of leaf midvein (PO_0020139).
Exact: a nectar-secreting gland is a nectary. Use the general class because the examples ('bearing 2-3 nectar glands') do not say whether it is floral or extrafloral.

target: peduncle (PO_0009053) part of spike inflorescence (PO_0030117), pattern 12
reason: The peduncle of a spike. Pattern 12 expresses it as a part of a qualified whole. In PO the peduncle is part of the inflorescence axis.

The margin of a stem leaf: 'stem' is already a context word giving cauline for leaf, plus the margin region. Using leaf with the cauline position, as the positioned-parts table does, rather than cauline leaf (PO_0000013, which is a vascular leaf) also covers moss stem leaves. 'serrulate', 'crenulate' and 'plane' suggest a moss flora.
Exact in sense: the receptive region of the carpel is the stigma by PO's definition. 'truncada' and 'crowned with trichomes' describe it.

A 'columna estilar' is the connate styles. Its dilated, lobate or discoid apex is the apex region of the style. If the flora is Apocynaceae this is the style head (FLOPO_0986079), so check the family.

target: underleaf; the segment as its lobe
label: underleaf
parent: is_a PO_0025075 (non-vascular leaf); part_of non-vascular leafy gametophyte stem
definition: A non-vascular leaf (PO:0025075) of a leafy liverwort that forms the ventral row on the stem. It usually differs in size and shape from the two lateral rows of leaves.
reason: A real liverwort structure with no class in PO or FLOPO. It is used by every leafy-liverwort flora, not just this one. 'Segment' is the lobe of the underleaf and can then be expressed as a lobe of underleaf. Should be proposed to PO upstream.

target: capsule fruit (PO_0030091) + region base; in moss descriptions sporangium base (PO_0030040)
reason: The base region of a capsule. 'base frecuentemente atenuada' fits a seed-plant capsule, but also a moss capsule narrowing into the seta. The moss-family rule should send bryophyte records to sporangium base.

target: emergence (FLOPO_0986107) part of orchid labellum (FLOPO_0980978), pattern 12
reason: An outgrowth borne on the labellum ('estipitado', 'ovoide', 'pubescente'). The labellum class exists. With no general appendage class, emergence part of the labellum is the closest expression. Too few records for its own class.
The lower side of the leaf (Spanish 'envés'), handled by the surface pattern like 'lower surface' and 'beneath'. It corresponds to leaf abaxial epidermis (PO_0006019).

Narrower: a pulvinule is the pulvinus at the base of a leaflet's petiolule. PO has petiole and leaf-sheath pulvini but no petiolule pulvinus, so map to the general pulvinus. A petiolule pulvinus class could be suggested to PO.

target: emergence (FLOPO_0986107) part of orchid labellum (FLOPO_0980978), pattern 12
reason: A raised, anchor-shaped, laterally flattened outgrowth near the lip apex is an orchid callus or appendage. Same treatment as 'labellum appendix'. If the flora is Lamiaceae or Acanthaceae, the whole would be corolla lip (FLOPO_0985017) instead.
Exact: the positioned part already exists (flower + position lower). It lists lower floret as a narrow synonym, which fits the grass spikelets here ('male', 'absent').
'abaxial surface' is already a surface context word. It corresponds to sepal abaxial epidermis (PO_0006054).

label: stomatal crypt
parent: is_a PO_0025376 (portion of plant tissue) to be confirmed against PO, or a FLOPO anatomical-space class; part_of PO_0006016 (leaf epidermis)
definition: A depression in the leaf epidermis, often lined with trichomes, at whose bottom one or more stomatal complexes (PO:0002000) open.
reason: A real anatomical structure (Nerium, Banksia, xeromorphic leaves) with no PO class. Only one flora uses it and some records are mis-parsed ('29 m high'), so do not add it yet. Propose it to PO upstream if a second flora needs it. The parent ID was not looked up and must be checked before use.
Narrower or related: the orifice of the corolla tube is its mouth, the throat region. Bare 'orifice' was rejected as generic, but here the organ is named. Only width and diameter are attached.

target: floral disc (FLOPO_0986025) part of pistillate flower (PO_0025599), pattern 12
reason: The disc of the female flower, as in 'calyx of male flowers' (pattern 12). Both classes exist.
Ambiguous: persistent fibres 0.2 mm wide are remains of leaf sheaths or leaf margins (palms, Yucca, Agave), not plant fiber cells (PO_0025407). The organ they come from is not named.

target: lamina (PO_0025060) + region margin; leaf lamina margin (PO_0025009) when the described organ is the leaf
reason: The margin of a blade ('ciliée', 'entire', 'toothed'). In floras it is nearly always the leaf blade, but lamina is generic in PO. The margin region on the lamina of the described organ keeps this correct for bracts and petals.

target: stamen (PO_0009029) part of staminate flower (PO_0025600), pattern 12
reason: The stamens of male flowers ('étamines 10-20' in the male-flower paragraph). Sex inheres in the flower, not the stamen (flora_context_words), so this is the part of a qualified whole.
Exact: 'middle pinna' is already an exact synonym of the positioned part median pinna.

target: pseudoperianth (FLOPO_0986118); lobes via count of parts (pattern 03) or as lobe part of pseudoperianth
reason: A lobe of the liverwort pseudoperianth. The class exists. 'lobes 8-12' is a count on the pseudoperianth, and colour or 'hyaline' go to the pseudoperianth's lobes. Not perianth lobe (FLOPO_0986004), which belongs to flowers.
A grass floret in a reduced state. The bearer is spikelet floret, and 'rudimentary' is a state of the bearer (PATO vestigial), so no new class is needed. Count and size attach to the floret.
Exact: the plural of samara, which is in PO as samara fruit.

Narrower: blue, ciliate, elliptic wings narrowing towards the pedicel are the two petaloid lateral (inner) sepals of Polygalaceae. They are sepals, not a wing on a sepal. Should not ground to wing petal (PO_0025325).
Exact: an abbreviation of tepal ('tep white, oblong, acute').
